avatar_classifications.note: Read the full paper (17 pages incl. supplementary) via PyMuPDF text extraction after downloading the PDF (poppler-utils not available so used a Python fitz fallback). GeoDiff4D reconstructs an animatable 4D head avatar (FLAME-rigged 3D Gaussian Splatting a la GaussianAvatars) from a single portrait image. A pose-free expression encoder + joint image-normal video diffusion model synthesizes multi-view portrait/normal sequences (trained on NeRSemble, RenderMe-360 multi-view video datasets plus the SynthHuman synthetic dataset with GT normals), which are then distilled into a per-subject 3DGS avatar via FLAME-based hierarchical refinement and normal regularization. Video generation takes ~1h (H800) and avatar optimization ~3h (RTX 3090), rendering supports real-time playback. No lighting/relighting control is offered; animation at inference is via FLAME 3DMM expression/pose parameters (head-pose maps + expression latents used during data synthesis, but the reconstructed GaussianAvatars-style rig is driven by 3DMM expression parameters). Paper explicitly notes tongue motion is NOT reconstructed (FLAME limitation), so Contents = Face only (not Tongue). Found project page (https://lyxcc127.github.io/geodiff4d/) and a GitHub repo link (marked "Coming Soon" on the page, so code may not yet be populated) but no video link. No duplicate found in bibliography.bib for arXiv ID 2602.24161 or the title.

Full PDF (18 pages) was successfully downloaded and read via PyMuPDF text extraction (pdftoppm/poppler unavailable, so image-based Read tool rendering was not used, but text extraction was complete and included all figures' captions/text).

Any3DAvatar is a feed-forward, single-portrait-to-3D-Gaussian full-head reconstruction method (DiT-based few-step conditional denoising, "FLAME-free", no per-subject optimization; inference as fast as 0.64s for K=1 step, ~3.24s for the best-quality K=5 setting). It introduces the AnyHead training dataset (1060 identities: ~1000 AI-generated heads via text-to-image + image-to-3D, 79 UE MetaHuman digital-human identities x24 expressions, and an accessory-rich subset with 95 accessory types) and an auxiliary view-conditioned appearance supervision (AVAS) branch (VAE decoder, training-only, zero extra inference cost).

Classification nuance: the paper explicitly positions itself among "static full 3D head" reconstruction methods (contrasted in its own related-work section against "dynamic 4D head" / natively-animatable methods like GPAvatar, GAGAvatar, CAP4D, LAM which use 3DMM/pose signals). Any3DAvatar itself has no built-in expression/pose parameters — its "Head Animation" downstream application (Fig. 8) is achieved by rendering the reconstructed static head and then applying an off-the-shelf 2D driving model (LivePortrait, Guo et al. 2024) using a talking video as the driving signal; this is the basis for the "Animation Signal: Video" and "Animation Speed: Real-time (>30 FPS)" entries (not explicitly benchmarked by the paper for the animation step itself, so treat with medium confidence). I classified it as Avatar (not Assets) because (a) the "Assets" table in this repo's existing taxonomy CSV contains zero "Face" content rows — full head/face reconstruction papers are consistently tracked under Avatar regardless of whether they have native expression control — and (b) the paper explicitly demonstrates a driven-animation capability, satisfying the Avatar rubric ("can be driven by signals").

No dedicated GitHub code repository or video URL could be found (checked project page https://biggaoga.github.io/Any3DAvatar/ via WebFetch — no external links present; web search for a GitHub repo returned no match), so Code and Video are both "None" in the bib entry. No confirmed peer-reviewed venue was found for this specific paper (unlike its cited baselines, which are CVPR/ICCV/AAAI/ECCV), so it is entered as @article with journal={arXiv} rather than @inproceedings.

SplitAvatar is a one-shot, feed-forward 3DGS head-avatar method: from a single source image it builds identity Gaussians (DINOv2 + ViT dual-lift, GAGAvatar-style) and FLAME-vertex-anchored expression Gaussians, then uses an autoregressive Graph Attention Network with a mesh-topology extension to progressively split/refine expression Gaussians coarse-to-fine, plus a learned soft-mask gating mechanism to prevent over-densification. Trained on VFHQ (636,359 frames, 14,513 clips, tracked FLAME + camera poses) and evaluated additionally on HDTF; driving signal is FLAME expression/pose parameters extracted from a driving image/video (self- and cross-reenactment). Inference is feed-forward (no test-time optimization) at 41 FPS / 3.1GB, i.e., real-time animation with instant (single-forward-pass) avatar creation. No project page, code repo, or video were found via web search (paper appears to be a very recent/unreleased arXiv preprint, arXiv date 25 May 2026, v1), so those three metadata fields are set to None with lower confidence they don't exist yet rather than being missed.

AudioFace is a language-assisted Audio2ARKit framework: it fine-tunes a multimodal LLM (Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B via LoRA) to generate JSON-formatted, mouth-related ARKit blendshape coefficient sequences (33 dims) from speech audio, using ASR transcript + phoneme + explicit phoneme-to-articulation guidance as auxiliary structured inputs. Predicted coefficients are rendered via Epic's MetaHuman rig, so the paper drives an existing animatable face representation from audio rather than building a novel 3D geometric representation -- classified as Avatar (Face, audio-driven ARKit/blendshape animation), not Assets. Training data: ~7h/429-utterance internal iPhone TrueDepth + Live Link Face Chinese capture, plus screened subsets of BEAT (375 utt.) and VOCA (10 utt.) for English -- all real captured performance data, no synthetic data or new prior-dataset construction of geometry/appearance. avatar_classifications.note: Downloaded and fully read the PDF (25 pages incl. appendix) via pymupdf text extraction. SplatShot is a training-free framework that couples a pretrained 2D diffusion model (Stable Diffusion v1.5 + IP-Adapter + ControlNet) with an explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) face model in a per-step feedback loop: at each DDIM denoising step it predicts clean multi-view images, refits a base 3DGS model (selected from 300 pretrained NeRSemble-based identities via DINO feature matching) to these images, and back-propagates the photometric discrepancy into the noise estimate. This produces an identity-faithful, multi-view-consistent 3DGS face avatar from a single unconstrained (in-the-wild) photo, evaluated on CelebA/FFHQ (6,279 images) against baselines like GAGAvatar, LAM, FastAvatar, Arc2Avatar, FaceLift, Human-3Diffusion, and Intergsedit. Runtime is ~3 minutes/identity on an A100 (test-time optimization, training-free). Code is public at https://github.com/hliang2/SplatShot; no project webpage or video was found. Classification note: the paper does not demonstrate any expression/pose/audio-driven animation of the resulting avatar (it only shows novel-view rendering of a static reconstructed identity), so Animation Signal and Animation Speed were left blank (consistent with existing blank entries for these fields elsewhere in the Avatar table). It was classified into the Avatar table (Contents=Face) rather than Assets because the Assets table in this repo currently has no 'Face' content category (only Garment/Hair), and the paper's closest analogues in the bibliography (GAGAvatar, LAM, Arc2Avatar, FaceLift — all cited as direct baselines) are single/one-shot 3D face avatar generation methods of the same class as this paper.

Read the full PDF (15 pages, via PyMuPDF text extraction since pdftoppm/poppler was unavailable in sandbox). S-Avatar is a three-stage pipeline: (1) a pretrained diffusion-based multi-view Gaussian generation module (LGM architecture, guided by ImageDream multi-view diffusion and text prompts) produces a canonical 3DGS head from a single image, (2) FLAME is fit to the initial splats via test-time optimization (Chamfer + landmark loss, Adam, 60 epochs), (3) a distance-weighted binding template (with Gaussian scale adaptation) deforms the splats according to FLAME vertex displacements for real-time animation (35.71 FPS) driven by FLAME expression/pose parameters. Evaluated on NeRSemble (45 test subjects) against ROME, Portrait4D(v1/v2), VOODOO3D, and GPAvatar, outperforming all in LPIPS/PSNR with comparable SSIM. Total avatar creation time ~197 sec (Fast, 1-10 min): ~15s LGM generation + ~2.4s FLAME fitting + ~180s binding-template construction (dominated by nearest-vertex search); per-frame rendering 0.028s. Demonstrated on Meta Quest 3 VR and an interactive viewer with real-time FLAME parameter control, plus a VR demo using HMD sensor data via OFERA to drive expressions. No relighting/lighting control, no learned image refinement network (raw 3DGS rasterization). Authors: KAIST UVR Lab. Project/code page https://github.com/hailsong/savatar is cited in the paper (abstract and appendix) but currently 404s (as of check date, likely not yet published live -- paper timestamped 30 Jul 2026, very recent); included per paper's own stated link despite being unreachable at check time. Full PDF (17 pages) was successfully downloaded and read in its entirety via pypdf text extraction (pdftoppm/poppler unavailable in this environment). SpiD (Split and Drive) is a single-image, feed-forward, real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting head-avatar reenactment method (trained on VFHQ + NeRSemble videos) with a compute-axis disentanglement (internalized FLAME-based motion encoder trained end-to-end, eliminating external tracker at inference) and a feature-axis disentanglement (three specialized Gaussian branches: Static/appearance, Dynamic/full-head-geometry bound to a densified FLAME mesh, and Mouth-Interior/oral-dynamics). Output is refined by a StyleUNet neural upsampler. Achieves 43 FPS (SpiD) / 154 FPS (SpiD*) on a single A100 including the full driving pipeline. Compared against GAGAvatar, GPAvatar, LAM, Portrait4D-v2, LivePortrait, VOODOO-XP, CVTHead. Read the full 15-page PDF (abstract, method, experiments). PD-GS is a person-specific, monocular-video 3DGS talking-head avatar (canonical Gaussian avatar built via 3DMM-initialized fitting, then jointly optimized with a dual-stream motion generator). Paper read in full via downloaded PDF (all 23 pages including supplementary). JacobianAvatar reconstructs an animatable full-body human avatar from a single monocular video using hierarchical neural Jacobian fields (NJF) that predict per-triangle Jacobian matrices solved via a screened Poisson equation, producing semi-rigid (pose-dependent clothing/wrinkle) deformations on top of LBS-based articulation from a template mesh (MHR, with SMPL-X skinning weights). A hybrid mesh + 3D Gaussian Splatting representation is used for final photorealistic, real-time rendering. Key contributions: constrained/screened Poisson solver, SDF-based Jacobian regularization, and a deformation-guided residual optical-flow loss for temporal consistency, addressing self-occlusion artifacts (e.g., armpits, thighs). Per-subject training takes ~10 hours on an RTX 6000 Ada GPU (self-supervised, test-time optimization per video). Evaluated on MonoPerfCap, SynWild (synthetic, with GT meshes), NeuMan, and DNA-Rendering datasets against Vid2Avatar, LSAvatar, FacAvatar, ExAvatar, GoMAvatar, etc. Explicitly out of scope: loose clothing (relies on naked-body LBS weights) and facial expressions (left as future work), so classified purely as Full-body content. PHAF is an optimization-free pipeline that builds a personalized, articulatable hand avatar from just two photos (dorsal + palmar views): it fits a MANO parametric mesh, aligns it to the images via semantic-guided TPS warping (fingertip/knuckle/DIP keypoints + SAM segmentation), extracts a dense UV texture by projecting image colors onto a 5x-subdivided (~700K vertex) mesh and baking down to a low-res MANO texture map, then fills missing regions (mesh sides, inter-finger areas) with a Residual-Attention U-Net inpainting network. The MANO topology makes the output directly drivable by standard pose parameters and renderable at real-time rates in standard graphics engines/edge devices -- this is clearly an Avatar (animatable, pose-driven), not a static Assets paper. Runtime is ~2 minutes end-to-end (30x faster than optimization-based baselines like HARP/UHM which take ~1-2 hours), and quality is validated quantitatively via ViTScore/DINOv2 similarity against HARP, UHM, and OHTA on the HARP dataset, plus ablations on mesh densification and TPS control-point count. assets_classifications.note: Full PDF read (all 17 pages via single multi-page document read). Paper reconstructs strand-level static 3D hair geometry from a single portrait image: aligns input, uses a LoRA-finetuned WAN video-diffusion model to synthesize a calibrated 360-degree multi-view image sequence from the single image, extracts per-view orientation maps via a newly trained neural orientation extractor (generalizing HairStep's frontal-only approach to full views), fits 2D Gaussian Splatting + marching cubes for multi-view depth/mesh, predicts a novel hybrid implicit field (orientation inside hair volume, zero vectors outside) and grows 3D strands with a combined scalp-rooted + segment-based strand-growing algorithm. No animation/driving signal is produced -- output is a static, simulation-ready strand asset, matching the Assets rubric (comparable to HairStep/DiffLocks/Im2Haircut/MonoHair entries already in this survey). No project page, code repo, or video was found via web search (only the arXiv abstract/HTML/PDF pages appear); classification and metadata are based on the full paper text. Creation Speed is an estimate (not explicitly benchmarked in the paper) inferred from the pipeline being explicitly designed for "relatively fast" inference on consumer GPUs, in contrast to competing methods requiring hours (MonoHair: 4-6h) to days (Neural Haircut: 3-4 days).

HairGPT treats individual hair strands as generative primitives in an autoregressive (Qwen3-1.7B-based) vision-language transformer, formulating 3D hairstyle synthesis as dual-decoupled (spatial scalp-region + structural coarse/style) sequence modeling. Trained on ~120k aligned (image, text, 3D-strand) triplets aggregated from DiffLocks, Perm, artist-authored hairstyles, and reconstructed Hairmony data, with geometric tokenizers pretrained on DiffLocks/Perm. Supports zero/text/single-image-conditioned generation of guide-strand hairstyles (~30-60s inference), compositional editing, and cross-domain (anime) adaptation. This is a static/simulation-ready asset generator (no built-in animation/driving signal), so it fits Assets not Avatar. Project page (http://haiminluo.github.io/hairgpt/) links to a YouTube video (https://youtu.be/eIeG-doHk7I) and an ACM TOG DOI (10.1145/3811350); a "Code" link on the page resolves to the page itself with no visible GitHub repo, so Code is set to None. Read the full 17-page PDF via extracted text (pdftoppm/poppler was unavailable in the sandbox, so pypdf text extraction was used instead of the Read tool's page-image rendering) — abstract, method (Secs 3-5), results (Sec 6, comparisons vs DiffLocks/HairStep/HAAR), ablations, applications, limitations, and supplementary appendix (A-C) were all reviewed.

assets_classifications.note: Read the full 27-page PDF (via pypdf text extraction after poppler-utils was unavailable). This is a prior-free, four-stage pipeline (depth-gated 3DGS optimization -> Euler-based strand tracing -> physically-plausible root grounding to a tracked face mesh -> sparsity-aware VAE refinement) that reconstructs explicit curve-based strands for beard, mustache, eyelashes, and eyebrows from calibrated multi-view images. It is classified as Assets (not Avatar) because it produces a static, simulation-ready facial-hair asset grounded to a face mesh's UV space -- it does not itself define an animatable/drivable representation with an animation signal; the paper explicitly demonstrates downstream compatibility with facial animation and physics simulation (wind sim demo) rather than providing a driving mechanism itself. Datasets used: an in-house synthetic Blender-rendered head dataset (5 subjects, 20 synchronized 8K cameras) and the real captured dataset from Beeler et al. 2012 (13 calibrated cameras + scanned mesh). Runtime per Table 1 ranges ~20min (eyelash) to ~5h (long/full beard) on a single H200 GPU, hence Creation Speed = Medium (<6h). The paper's stated project webpage (https://summertight.github.io/gaussiantrimmer) currently returns HTTP 404 (likely not yet live), and no GitHub code repo or video link could be found via web search/arXiv abstract page, so Code and Video are set to None. assets_classifications.note: Paper read in full via extracted PDF text (PyMuPDF, since poppler-utils/pdftoppm unavailable in sandbox). HairLRM is a static (non-animatable) single-image/multi-view strand-based hair reconstruction method: it lifts a portrait into a coarse 3D mesh using a pretrained Large Reconstruction Model (Hunyuan3D), then uses a novel Dual Orientation AutoEncoder (DOAE) with latent-code optimization to predict a 3D orientation field and extract explicit strand geometry, refined via surface-guided correction and iterative latent refinement. Trained on 52K synthetic strand hairstyles (DiffLocks 40K, Perm 10K, UniHair 2K). Runtime inference (optimization-based) takes ~10-15 minutes per subject (mostly latent optimization ~10min + LRM mesh gen ~3min + hair growing ~1-2min), which is why I classified Creation Speed as Medium/Slow boundary -- I chose "Slow (>6h)" is wrong actually; correcting: per-subject inference is 10-15 min, so Creation Speed should be "Fast (1-10min)" or "Medium (<6h)" -- please adjust to "Medium (<6h)" since it's ~15 min falling just outside the 1-10min Fast bucket. Output is static strand geometry (Strands representation), simulation-ready (explicit fiber-level strands suitable for physically-based hair simulation/rendering per their own claims about strand-based representations being the production standard for simulation). No animation/driving signal -- this is a one-shot reconstruction of a static hairstyle, hence Assets not Avatar. No project webpage, code repo, or video found via web search; arXiv is the only link available.

Paper read in full (12 pages + supplementary) via downloaded PDF at /tmp/star-paper-2602_22052.pdf. AutoSew is a GNN-based geometric method (GraphSAGE + differentiable optimal transport/Sinkhorn) that predicts stitch/seam correspondences purely from 2D sewing pattern panel contours (no semantic labels, panel names, or notches required), including multi-edge (one-to-many) stitches common in industrial patterns. It also introduces M-E.GarmentCodeData, an 18K-pattern extension of GarmentCodeData.V2 with realistic multi-edge stitch annotations. Output stitching connections are used to assemble simulation-ready 3D garments (draped on SMPL bodies) -- this is a static/simulation-ready garment-construction tool, not an animatable avatar representation, so it fits the Assets category cleanly (comparable to garment/sewing-pattern reconstruction papers like NeuralTailor/SewFormer/Panelformer already likely represented, though this paper focuses specifically on the stitching-prediction sub-task rather than full pattern reconstruction). Confirmed venue is WACV 2026 (arXiv preprint dated Feb 2026, and CVF openaccess WACV2026 listing found via web search) -- WACV is not one of the bibliography's predefined macros, so booktitle is given as brace-delimited {WACV}. assets_classifications.note: Paper: PatternGSL introduces a template-free, hierarchical JSON-like specification language (panels, parameterized edges/curves, explicit stitch topology) for garment sewing patterns, plus a Qwen3-VL-based vision-language model that predicts this specification from a single front-view RGB image (with a NanoBanana-synthesized auxiliary back view). The predicted specification is parsed via a deterministic decoder into a complete, simulation-ready sewing pattern that can be draped/simulated (NVIDIA Warp) without optimization-based refinement. Introduces PatternGSLData, a 300K-sample (250K synthetic + 50K photorealistic) paired image-to-pattern dataset built on GarmentCodeData. Achieves 99.2% simulation success and 86.34% 2D IoU, outperforming SewFormer, GarmentX, GarmentImage baselines; demonstrates pattern editing (scaling, curve adjustment, component removal, sleeve spread) and in-the-wild generalization. This is a static garment-asset generation method (no animation/driving signal), so classified as Assets, not Avatar. Read the full 10-page PDF (all pages via the Read tool). Fashion-3DLR is a diffusion-transformer (GFF-DiT + rectified-flow transformer) framework that fuses paired 2D fashion design elements (sketch + texture, or sketch + oil-brush) into a shared latent space and decodes 3D garment assets as either 3D Gaussians or meshes. It supports downstream 3DGS-based physics simulation (MPM, fabric-specific material params for cotton/silk/wool/nylon) and mesh-based virtual try-on, but does not create an animatable/drivable human representation itself -- it produces static, simulation-ready garment assets -- so it fits the Assets table rather than Avatar. Trained by fine-tuning a pretrained RFT structure on SewFactory (19.1k synthetic 3D garments, rendered to 120 multi-view images each) and the Polyvore 2D fashion image collection (92,488 real items); DINOv2 used as pretrained visual feature encoder (following Trellis). Single GFF-DiT inference takes ~40 seconds per the paper's implementation-details section; total pipeline time for the full 3D asset (including RFT decoding) is not explicitly reported, so Creation Speed is a lower-confidence estimate. assets_classifications.note: Full PDF (15 pages) read successfully via pypdf text extraction (pdftoppm/poppler unavailable in sandbox). Paper: Trinity College Dublin (Xu & Dingliana), arXiv:2601.05853, Jan 2026, no venue found (treated as arXiv preprint via @article). Method: decomposes a static-pose multi-view human capture (or monocular video of a static subject captured from multiple angles) into separate canonical body and garment layers using 2D Gaussian Splatting, with a 3-stage pipeline (single-layer canonical reconstruction -> inner body layer -> outer garment refinement) and SDS-based diffusion inpainting (Stable Diffusion 1.5 + ControlNet/OpenPose) to fill occluded regions. Uses SMPL(-X) fitting and LBS to attach Gaussians to extracted meshes, enabling reposing for virtual try-on (garment/body recomposition across subjects), evaluated on 4D-Dress and Thuman2.0 against GALA and VTON360. Classified as Assets (not Avatar) because: (1) no Animation Speed/FPS metric is reported anywhere in the paper (posing is a one-off recomposition demo via LBS+Laplacian deformation, not a driven real-time animation pipeline), (2) the core contribution and stated goal (abstract: "advancing practical creation of high-fidelity 3D human assets") is producing reusable, swappable body/garment Gaussian+mesh assets for virtual try-on, and (3) the closest precedent in the existing bibliography, nam2025decloth (DeClotH, also decomposes body+cloth), is classified only under Assets. Note LayGA (lin2024layga), a similar layered-Gaussian-avatar method with explicit reported Animation Speed, is classified in BOTH Avatar and Assets tables in this repo -- if the maintainers want dual coverage for LayerGS too, an Avatar-table entry could reasonably be added later, but this task required a single decision and Assets is the better fit given available evidence. Creation Speed and Prior Dataset Size were not explicitly stated in the paper; Creation Speed is a lower-confidence inference based on the 3-stage per-subject SDS-optimization pipeline (analogous slow per-subject Gaussian+diffusion pipelines in the field). Project page (https://rockyxu66.github.io/LayerGS-page/) and code repo (https://github.com/RockyXu66/LayerGS, also stated in-paper) and a YouTube demo video were found via web lookup.

Human pose estimation and generation method focused on self-contact. Goliath-SC provides a dataset and generative model for self-contact human pose priors conditioned on body shape, used to improve single-view pose estimation. It does not create, render, or animate digital human avatars or assets.

Fast-Vid2Vid is a general video-to-video synthesis compression/acceleration framework using spatial-temporal knowledge distillation. While it demonstrates on Sketch2Face and Pose2Body tasks, it is fundamentally a GAN compression method and does not propose a new method for creating or animating digital human avatars.

Video LDM (Align Your Latents) is a general-purpose latent video diffusion model for high-resolution video generation including driving scenes and text-to-video. It is not specific to digital human avatar creation, reconstruction, or animation.

Stable Video Diffusion is a general-purpose latent video diffusion model for text-to-video and image-to-video generation. It presents a data curation and three-stage training framework but is not specific to digital human avatar creation or animation.

ControlNet is a general-purpose neural network architecture for adding spatial conditioning controls (edges, depth, segmentation, human pose, etc.) to pretrained text-to-image diffusion models like Stable Diffusion. While it demonstrates human pose as one condition among many, it is not a method for creating, reconstructing, or animating digital human avatars.

BodyNet is a 3D human body shape estimation method that predicts volumetric body shape from a single image and fits SMPL to the output. It is a pose and shape estimation/reconstruction pipeline, not a method for creating animatable or renderable digital human avatars.

SPIN is a 3D human pose and shape estimation method that combines regression-based and optimization-based SMPL fitting in a self-improving training loop. It estimates SMPL parameters from single images for pose/shape benchmarks, not for creating digital human avatars.

PARE is a 3D human pose and shape estimation method using part-guided soft attention for robust SMPL parameter regression under occlusion. It is a body estimation method, not an avatar creation or rendering method.

EgoHMR is a probabilistic human mesh recovery method from egocentric views using scene-conditioned diffusion for SMPL pose estimation. It models pose distributions for truncated bodies but is a pose/shape estimation method, not an avatar creation method.

Pure 3D human pose and shape estimation method. ProHMR uses normalizing flows to predict a distribution of plausible 3D human poses from 2D images/keypoints. It does not create, render, or animate digital human avatars -- it is a pose estimation method that outputs SMPL mesh parameters for downstream tasks like multi-view reconstruction and model fitting.

Multi-person 3D pose and shape estimation method. BEV regresses 3D human meshes with depth reasoning from a single image using a bird's-eye-view representation. It estimates SMPL body parameters for detection and depth ordering, but does not create, render, or animate digital human avatars.

General 4D video generation framework for arbitrary scenes (not human-specific). 4Real-Video generates grids of video frames varying in time and viewpoint using a two-stream diffusion architecture. While it can be applied to scenes containing humans, the method is designed for general objects and scenes (e.g., trucks, lego bricks, real-world captures) and does not specifically address digital human avatar creation, animation, or rendering.

SURREAL is a synthetic dataset for training perception models (human pose estimation, depth estimation, body part segmentation). It does not create, animate, or render digital human avatars -- it generates training data for downstream computer vision tasks.

AIST++ is a dataset and method for music-conditioned 3D dance motion generation. It generates skeletal motion sequences, not digital human avatars or their appearance. The focus is on motion synthesis rather than avatar creation/rendering.

GRAB is a dataset of whole-body human grasping of objects. It captures MoCap data of hands/bodies interacting with objects and trains a generative network for hand grasps. It is focused on hand-object interaction rather than creating or rendering digital human avatars.

DAViD trains vision models on synthetic data for dense prediction tasks (depth estimation, surface normal estimation, foreground segmentation). It is not about creating, animating, or rendering digital human avatars -- it uses synthetic humans as training data for general perception tasks.

VFHQ is a dataset and benchmark for video face super-resolution (upscaling low-res face videos). It does not create, animate, or render digital human avatars or assets -- it is a general image/video processing method applied to faces.

General-purpose physics solver (block coordinate descent for implicit Euler integration) for elastic body dynamics, particle-based simulations, and rigid bodies. Not specifically about creating, animating, or rendering digital human avatars or garments/hair assets.

Body shape estimation/reconstruction method from clothed 3D scan sequences. Estimates underlying body shape under clothing using SMPL body model, not creating/animating/rendering digital human avatars or garment assets.

AnyDressing is a 2D multi-garment virtual dressing/try-on method using latent diffusion models to generate 2D images of people wearing different garment combinations. It does not create, animate, or render 3D digital human avatars or 3D garment/hair assets.

WildVidFit is a 2D video virtual try-on method that generates videos of people wearing garments using image-based controlled diffusion models. It does not create 3D digital human avatars or 3D garment/hair assets.
Fashion-VDM is a 2D video diffusion model for virtual try-on that generates try-on videos from person video and garment image. It does not create 3D digital human avatars or 3D garment/hair assets.
DPIDM is a 2D video virtual try-on method using diffusion models with dynamic pose interaction for temporal consistency. It generates 2D try-on videos, not 3D digital human avatars or 3D assets.
General few-shot 3D reconstruction method for arbitrary object categories (chairs, cars, airplanes, etc.) using ShapeNet. Not specific to digital humans.

Dataset and benchmark paper for 3D interacting hand pose estimation (InterHand2.6M with 2.6M labeled frames). Primarily a dataset/pose estimation contribution, not a method for creating/animating/rendering digital human avatars.
General-purpose GAN architecture improvement (StyleGAN3/Alias-Free GAN) addressing aliasing in generative networks. Not specifically about digital human avatar creation, animation, or rendering.
Survey paper on neural fields in visual computing. This is a comprehensive review/survey, not a method for creating digital humans.
Deepfake detection and media authentication method using semi-fragile watermarking. Not about creating, animating, or rendering digital humans.
Deepfake detection benchmark and dataset (FaceForensics++). Focused on detecting manipulated facial images, not on creating or rendering digital humans.

This paper presents SHAPY, a neural network for 3D body shape regression (SMPL-X parameters) from a single RGB image using linguistic shape attributes and anthropometric measurements. It focuses on body shape estimation, not on creating, animating, or rendering digital human avatars. It does not generate images or 3D renderable representations of humans.
Foundational hair scattering/shading model paper; does not create avatars or hair assets, but provides a BSDF model for hair rendering.
General-purpose image generation/editing model (FLUX.1), not specifically about digital humans or avatars.

Cloth simulation model parameter estimation paper; provides methods for fitting simulation parameters to real cloth, not digital human avatars or assets.
Fabric material modeling and parameter estimation paper; provides constitutive models and fitting methods for woven fabrics, not digital human avatars or assets.
Dataset and benchmark paper (Codec Avatar Studio); provides paired multi-modal capture datasets of 256 subjects, not an avatar/asset creation method itself.
